# Builds are signed with one key kept outside the repo

**Status:** accepted

**Context:** Updates (sideloaded or through depot's in-app updater) only install over an existing install signed with the same key; depot also pins an app's first signer.
**Decision:** Debug and release builds sign with `~/.android/blot.jks` (EC P-256, alias `blot`), created once per machine as the README says; an untracked `signing.properties` can point elsewhere. When the file is absent, builds fall back to the debug key.
**Alternatives:** The debug key — differs per machine and is regenerated by tooling, so updates would stop installing. A key in the repo — anyone with the source could sign an update.
**Consequences:** Losing the key means users reinstall (depot refuses another signer). Builds signed with the debug key, such as the first `app.blot` installs, don't update in place: uninstall them once.
